description.text:
Completed-vector storage internal to C2C, not an SRF stall mechanism.
DEPTH must be >= 2. No empty-to-output combinational fall-through.

Vector-level peer transport for the normal path, not a physical link.
A valid input available after edge C is visible at RX after edge C+L.
LINK_LATENCY must be >= 1; every stage advances each cycle, even bubbles.

Stateless FIFO-head rendezvous. Both upstream queues retain their heads
until pop; their heads are consumed together at the Replay sampling edge.
This is the proposed minimal Receive/ready-vector pairing contract.

Complete received vectors only. Destination selection belongs to Receive.
DEPTH >= 1. No empty-to-output combinational fall-through.

Normal-path expansion of one complete vector into four diagonal SRF
producer candidates. Collision handling and SRF selection are external.

description.text: Four-tile, normal-path diagonal gather. Stream selection is external.

Vector-level admission control between the completed FIFO and peer flight.
This is deliberately not a beat-level PHY serializer.  One accepted vector
holds one credit through serializer occupancy, link flight, and RX-ready
residence; the paired Receive pop supplies credit_return_i.

Single logical DMA Store-lane control context.
This block accepts already-decoded descriptor semantics.  It intentionally
does not decode a 192-bit descriptor slot, define an ICU codec, generate
addresses, or issue external-storage requests.  The fixed P_LANE_INDEX
identifies the logical DMA lane; it is distinct from an ordinary SRF stream
selector even when a static schedule uses the same numeric value.

instances.generateContext: for (genvar bank = 0; bank < F*2; bank = bank + 1)

description.text:
Phase 2B wrapper: a bank-local, zero-cycle command conversion in front of
the unchanged Phase 2A MEM/SRF data plane.

DMA-1C Store-only composition.  MEM and the DMA TX attachment share one
ordinary SRF hemisphere.  The wrapper owns no SRF payload state: leaf state
remains exclusively inside ftlpu_sr_superlane_col_dir.
The Store attachment is the existing C2C TX tap in External-storage DMA
mode: East sreg13, E0..E7, and local consumer slot 0.  It is deliberately
not a peer transport, descriptor engine, or external-memory protocol.

Phase 2A standalone MEM/SRF data-plane integration variant.
The adapter in this module is purely combinational.  The authoritative SRF
owns all stream state; MEM only observes current boundary state and produces
consume/inject candidates.  MEM uses two independent local candidate slots (Q06=A).

Phase 4A-2 adds no data-path state: it is the explicit full-round-trip
variant of the validated Phase 4A-1 shared-SRF integration.

Shared-SRF integration. MEM slots0/1 and SXM slot1 share disjoint columns
under Q06=A; this wrapper is entirely combinational outside the existing IP.

Stateless VMODEL-to-native SXM command translator.  It accepts only the
native-compatible subset of the existing 416-bit format and fails closed
for unsupported selector lists, maps, opcodes, or output-tile encodings.

Stateless SXM/SRF segment adapter.  It translates only packed bus layout
and the fixed SXM slot/boundary contract; it owns no payload or valid state.

Phase 3B command-path variant.  Phase 3A remains unchanged: this wrapper
only translates VMODEL 416-bit SXM controls into native 96-bit controls.
Native WriteTap scheduler. No payload registers; existing SRF captures wide P.

Four existing MEM groups, West at MEM_LEFT..MEM_LEFT-3; no new data queue.
Command observation pipeline carries metadata only, mirroring native hops.
Completion counts valid Tap samples, with target/address checks and fault gate.

description.text:
Metadata-only native command monitor and commit/drain accounting.
Command taps mirror the unchanged MEM hop; payload valid is observed at SRF.
Native WriteTap scheduler. No payload registers; existing SRF captures wide P.

Complete shared SXM + zero-payload native WriteTap shell.
Batch/MEM entry is MATRIX only; ROW/P/RUN and raw/API retain original ports.
Existing MEM/SRF provide observed valid/busy/fault, without payload copies.

One independent south-to-north command pipeline for a logical MEM bank.
Native command bit 30 selects a one-cycle (0) or three-cycle (1) hop.
tile0 sees the current south command combinationally. Each later tile has
one execution register and two extra registers used only by long commands.

One physical MEM storage leaf for a fixed
(hemisphere, mem_slice, bank, superlane) coordinate.
The SRAM array is single-port: at most one complete-row Read or Write is
accepted in a cycle. Reset clears only control/output state; SRAM contents
are intentionally not reset.

Stateless c7 raw primitive to native canonical command conversion.
This is not the legacy 47-bit packet format and adds no issue register.
The current parameterized input ABI extends c7 with delay3 in bit 30.
Set P_ALLOW_DELAY3=0 only when checking the frozen original c7 encoding.

Generic MEM group located between a left boundary (sreg[g]) and a right
boundary (sreg[g+1]). Four slices share the same cycle-start boundary state.

description.text:
One MEM hemisphere: 52 slices arranged as 13 fixed groups between 14 MEM
SR boundaries. This wrapper routes cycle-start state and candidates only; it
does not implement SR propagation or next-state commit.

IMPLEMENTATION CHOICE / INTERNAL INTEGRATION INTERFACE:
one logical bank composed of independent single-port SRAM leaves and a
command pipeline with per-command one/three-cycle hops (native bit 30).
This wrapper adds no storage and performs no bank-global arbitration.

One MEM slice contains two fully independent logical banks. The Slice/SR
boundary is abstract: it observes only the current boundary SR state and
emits consume/injection candidates. It does not instantiate or arbitrate SR.

description.text:
Weight-stationary Supercell. No dynamic scheduling or backpressure.
One activation vector broadcasts to every output group on the same edge.
Group n computes sum_k activation[k]*weight[buffer][n][k], with TERMS
multipliers per group. All groups have the same dot/partial output phase.
Activation, buffer ID, tag and valid forward right through ONE register;
the compiler arranges lower-partial inputs at simultaneous dot-valid.

Load-only INT8 -> BF16 conversion. D1 subtract/decode, D2 exact 8x8
product and normalization-shift detection. D3 shift/RNE feeds the Supercell
weight register, the third register boundary (no extra output register).
Parameter commands load paired scale/zero buffers; D1 snapshots their values.
Weight and parameter commands consume separate fixed byte streams. No general
FP32 multiplier, integer-to-BF16 intermediate, LUT or division is used.

source is ready and old enough. The supported profile is 4T x 16S.

Each source tile owns one independent single-entry 128-byte buffer. The

are combinational intents for the current cycle.

Arithmetic consumers see subnormal operands as signed zero (DAZ).  The raw
input remains outside this module so bit-preserving operations such as

One combinational FP32 Newton multiply stage. Finite operands use one
inferred unsigned 24x24 significand multiply inside fp32_multiply_rne.
Two instances keep the two Newton products on separate dedicated 24x24
significand datapaths:
  stage 1: m*y0
  stage 2: y0*(2-m*y0)
The current special-ALU issue controller remains single-outstanding; its
admission policy can be relaxed separately. The module boundary keeps the
two physical demand points explicit for DC.

Fused FP32 RSQRT Newton correction:
  correction = 1.5 - 0.5*m*y_squared
m and y_squared are positive finite normal FP32 values on this internal
path. Their 24x24 significand product remains at full 48-bit precision,
is aligned with 1.5 in Q55, subtracted, and rounded to FP32 only once.

One logical VXM Queue Frontend: packet buffering, RUN_2D decode, Context
buffering, absolute-cycle expansion and deadline-qualified Compact issue.

Fixed-point RECIP LUT interpolation for y0 = b - k*dx.
A 64-entry table consumes the top six fraction bits as its address. The
remaining fraction bits are a right-aligned residual:
  BF16: 1 bit / 2^7, FP16: 4 bits / 2^10, FP32: 17 bits / 2^23.
k and b are physically UQ1.15. Narrow formats use RNE-reduced UQ1.9 and
UQ1.12 values. One 16x17 unsigned multiply is shared by zero extension;
the aligned subtraction uses one signed 40-bit datapath.
待确认：RTL 结构显示 6 个输入、3 个输出，并包含 0 个子模块实例模板。该说明仅来自结构计数，未推断功能。

Fixed-point RSQRT LUT interpolation for y0 = b - k*dx.
The 64-entry address is {exponent parity, five high fraction bits}.
The parity-dependent factor of two is folded into the stored slope, leaving
right-aligned residuals of 2/5/18 bits for BF16/FP16/FP32 respectively.
k and b are physically UQ1.15. Narrow formats use RNE-reduced UQ1.9 and
UQ1.12 values. One zero-extended 16x18 multiply and one signed 40-bit
subtraction are shared by all formats.

One shared 27-bit significand add/subtract datapath, split at the FP16
boundary: 14 low bits and 13 high bits. The extra result bit is the carry,
not a 28th full-adder bit. BF16/FP16 isolate the high group completely.

description.text:
One format-selected FP16/BF16/FP32 add/subtract cone.
The format MUX and operand isolation are deliberately before the shared
significand datapath. Near subtraction uses one grouped leading-zero
encoder and one format-masked variable left shifter.

Shared FP16/BF16/FP32 magnitude and ordered comparator.
Operand format decode, classification and DAZ are performed once by the
Basic-ALU front end. This block only compares the resulting fields. FP16
and BF16 use the complete low 15-bit comparator. FP32 adds a high 16-bit
comparison and consults the same low comparator only when the high parts
are equal.

One logical left shifter shared by FP16, BF16 and FP32 normalization.
The format mask isolates unused high input bits and truncates the result.

Shared unsigned coefficient multiplier for LUT-based special functions.
The default EXP instance is a physical 26x24 multiply. Parameters also
permit narrower coefficient formats while retaining one physical datapath.
Narrow formats round the stored coefficient to their selected internal
precision, right-align the
active value significand, and zero-fill every unused high bit:
  BF16 : UQ1.9  (10 bits) x  8-bit significand
  FP16 : UQ1.12 (13 bits) x 11-bit significand
  FP32 : UQ1.25 (26 bits) x 24-bit significand
This deliberately leaves the multiplier architecture to synthesis/DC.

policy.statement: Physical Architecture 展示功能单元、hemisphere 拓扑与数据/控制关系；RTL Hierarchy 保留源码层次。
policy.accuracyStatement: 参考图只决定表达形式。实例数、阵列参数、generate 范围与接口证据均来自当前 RTL；未确认项保留表达式或 Needs Review。
policy.floorplanDisclaimer: 此视图不是最终芯片 floorplan，也不表示后端物理坐标或实际布线。

regions.name: External Program Memory Boundary
regions.basis: Current RTL exposes a generic Program DMA command/response boundary. No DDR controller, DDR memory model, or standard AXI five-channel adapter is instantiated in the authoritative RTL snapshot.

regions.name: Program Load and Distributed Instruction Control
regions.basis: The display separates the RTL-confirmed Instruction DMA, response reassembly, hemisphere distribution and FU-local instruction-control path. Relative placement is architectural, not floorplan data.

regions.name: West Hemisphere
regions.basis: HEMISPHERE_INDEX 1 is selected by gen_west_host_column; left/right presentation is a functional-topology view, not floorplan coordinates.

regions.name: Central / On-chip Bisection
regions.basis: The single VXM instance is outside the two-hemisphere generate loop and connects both MEM sides.

regions.name: East Hemisphere
regions.basis: HEMISPHERE_INDEX 0 is selected by gen_east_host_column; left/right presentation is a functional-topology view, not floorplan coordinates.

blocks.function: Native-default MEM with 104 paired bank-local instruction frontend + timed queue paths south of the bank array. Each paired path emits a MEM64 command northward into its logical bank control column; legality checks, private Native32 adaptation and bidirectional stream data remain explicit.
blocks.placementBasis: The else branch is named gen_west_host_column; relative display order is a topology presentation, not physical coordinates.

rtlMappings.basis: Two-instance generate loop with an RTL-confirmed hemisphere selector.

controlPath: 104 paired local instruction frontend + timed queue paths
structure.namingNote: USE_NATIVE_MEM defaults to 1. Native32 exists only beyond the adapter boundary. The disabled Legacy Compatibility branch maps Bank0 into 52 old issue paths and turns Bank1 issue into an explicit sticky compatibility fault.

blocks.function: East/West stream pass-through, transpose storage and permutation routing.
blocks.placementBasis: The else branch is named gen_west_host_column; relative display order is a topology presentation, not physical coordinates.

rtlMappings.basis: SXM is instantiated inside the same confirmed hemisphere loop as MEM.

blocks.function: Two local MXM engines sharing the hemisphere stream boundary, with load, dequant and compute paths.
blocks.placementBasis: The else branch is named gen_west_host_column; relative display order is a topology presentation, not physical coordinates.

rtlMappings.basis: Nested generate loop instantiates two MXM subsystems per hemisphere.

blocks.function: Native-default MEM with 104 paired bank-local instruction frontend + timed queue paths south of the bank array. Each paired path emits a MEM64 command northward into its logical bank control column; legality checks, private Native32 adaptation and bidirectional stream data remain explicit.
blocks.placementBasis: HEMISPHERE_INDEX == 0 selects gen_east_host_column; relative display order is a topology presentation, not physical coordinates.

nodes.description: Issue/control, bidirectional stream boundary, pass-through, transpose and permutation organization. R0–R6 now reaches the real subsystem Program Boundary, but the endpoint still lacks local-iMEM / Fetch Adapter integration.
The R6 Outer Local boundary is real, but program_ready_o remains zero and no local-iMEM/fetch adapter connects Program Load to the resident issue path.

nodes.displayName: SXM 指令译码（架构概括）
nodes.description: Architectural grouping for the resident Transpose/Permute issue path. Standalone macro frontend RTL exists, but this label does not claim a same-named integrated decoder module.
RTL-confirmed stream ingress, pass registers, transpose capture bank, whole-bank permutation routing and stream egress.
R6 Outer Local reaches this real subsystem boundary. program_ready_o=0 and no Commit path is implemented.

sourceEvidence.basis: R6 Outer Local is decoded and presented to the SXM boundary.
SXM holds program_ready_o low.

nodes.description: No integrated transport converts the boundary record into resident SXM macro instructions.
Transpose and Permute Macro Frontend modules pass their standalone unit tests, but are not connected to Program Load.
Two independent 416-bit instruction channels enter the slice. Transpose walks four rows; Permute is one registered whole-bank operation.

sourceEvidence.basis: u_transpose_pipeline and the explicit Permute register own different timing geometries.

nodes.description: Each side exposes 4 Tiles × 32 Streams × 64 bits.
Uncaptured streams cross one registered boundary cycle in either direction. This is pass-through storage, not a shift engine.

sourceEvidence.basis: Uncaptured streams are written into east_pass_* or west_pass_* next-state registers.

nodes.description: A four-row 416-bit control wave captures sixteen selected streams per Tile into a 2-plane byte-register bank.

sourceEvidence.basis: transpose_bank_q is an explicit 8-bit register array; no SRAM module is instantiated.

nodes.description: One registered Permute instruction validates a 32-lane bijection, selects complete 8-lane Tile blocks and emits two planes per row.

nodes.description: The large layer frames are display containers, not extra RTL modules. The primary architecture view follows only the RTL data path: Instruction DMA → buffered response → reassembly/Assembler → Word FIFO, then Distributor Elastic Stage → central VXM direct endpoint or the West/East seven-stage Relay chains → FU-local frontend/local iMEM boundaries. Descriptor sequencing, PRIME selection, Scope/Destination decode and lifecycle state remain available one level below the corresponding stage instead of fragmenting the main chain.

sourceEvidence.basis: u_program_load_system is a direct top-level subsystem.
u_program_distribute_system is a direct top-level sibling and owns Distribution.
u_fu_subsystems owns each FU-local endpoint.
The load path instantiates Instruction DMA, Reassembler and Word FIFO in order.
The Distributor owns the only input Elastic Stage and feeds the direct VXM path plus two Relay chains.

nodes.displayName: 指令 DMA / Program Read DMA
nodes.description: Main-chain source. lpu_program_load_path instantiates lpu_instruction_dma, which accepts source address, byte count and DMA ID, drives the generic external read contract, reserves outstanding IDs and buffers returned beats.

sourceEvidence.basis: u_instruction_dma is the first payload stage inside the load path.
u_response_fifo buffers the complete external response record.

nodes.description: Controller support: writes one Program Command descriptor. This is metadata, not FU instruction payload storage.

sourceEvidence.basis: Program Load Controller owns command and lifecycle control.

nodes.description: Controller-owned Program Command storage supports the DMA path without replacing the payload main chain.
Controller support that emits the load transaction fields consumed by lpu_program_load_path.

sourceEvidence.basis: u_program_load_controller supplies the load-path transaction.

nodes.displayName: 响应缓冲 / DMA Response Buffer
nodes.description: Main-chain buffering boundary. The 16-entry response FIFO inside lpu_instruction_dma retains 256-bit data, keep, last, ID and error before the Reassembler consumes it. External DDR/AXI/C2C integration remains outside this RTL.

sourceEvidence.basis: u_response_fifo is the implemented DMA response buffer.

nodes.description: Main-chain reassembly stage. lpu_program_load_reassembler pairs image context with buffered response bytes, compacts valid bytes in a 64-byte reservoir and emits 96/128-bit logical Program Words on the 128-bit transport.

sourceEvidence.basis: u_reassembler consumes the buffered DMA response and config FIFO context.
The byte reservoir is the only state changed by simultaneous beat acceptance and word emission.

nodes.description: Pairs response bytes with Scope, Destination, format, local iMEM base and image metadata.

sourceEvidence.basis: u_config_fifo is accepted atomically with the DMA command.

nodes.description: Compacts response bytes selected by the keep mask and preserves partial instruction words across response beats.

sourceEvidence.basis: The explicit byte reservoir owns simultaneous beat acceptance and word emission state.

nodes.description: Consumes 12 or 16 compacted bytes and emits a fixed 128-bit transport word with strobe 0111 or 1111 plus routing sideband.

Explicit boundary between Program Load and Program Distribution. The eight-entry FIFO stores the 164-bit record: 128-bit data + 4-bit strobe + 2-bit Scope + 12-bit Destination + 17-bit iMEM address + last.

sourceEvidence.basis: u_word_fifo follows the Reassembler and drives load_word_*.
The dedicated Word FIFO wraps the shared queue FIFO.

nodes.description: First stage owned by lpu_program_distributor. It buffers the complete 165-bit record before central-VXM direct selection or West/East Relay-chain routing.

sourceEvidence.basis: u_load_record_elastic is the Distributor input stage.

nodes.description: Controller support defers PRIME until instruction loading completes.
Selects a Word FIFO WRITE record or deferred PRIME record before the Distributor input.

nodes.displayName: 指令接力链 / Relay Chain · West + East
nodes.description: Two RTL-confirmed seven-stage chains, W0–W6 and E0–E6. Each stage owns two-entry transport and a fixed MEM Bank range; R6 also forwards the outer MXM/SXM record. VXM does not enter either Relay chain.

sourceEvidence.basis: Two generated Relay chains instantiate u_program_relay_chain.
VXM direct and Relay-chain inputs are independent routes.

nodes.description: The Distributor expands EAST/WEST/BOTH and emits concrete endpoint records before Relay entry.
Concrete West record feeds W0 directly.
Concrete East record feeds E0 directly.

MEM and MXM terminate in integrated local iMEM/frontends. SXM and VXM expose real Program boundaries but their local load adapters remain unintegrated; the diagram marks those endpoints without inventing transport.

sourceEvidence.basis: MEM local frontends consume the Relay-local Program ports.
MXM local frontends consume outer Program records.
SXM boundary currently holds Ready low.
VXM boundary currently holds Ready low.

nodes.description: Lifecycle and reset support remain explicit one level below the endpoint summary.
MEM and MXM accept Program writes into their local frontend/iMEM paths.

nodes.displayName: SXM / VXM Boundary · Endpoint Not Integrated
nodes.description: SXM/VXM Program ports are wired to the subsystem boundary, but Ready remains low and no local iMEM adapter or Commit path is implemented.

Integrated Queue-control system: a shared record Pool feeds one Cache and one five-state Controller per formal endpoint, then scheduler_counter_ce drives the FU-local Scheduler Cycle Counter. ENABLE_QCTL defaults to zero, so the structure is RTL-integrated but default-gated.

sourceEvidence.basis: gen_queue_endpoint creates one Queue Cache and one Controller for each formal endpoint.

nodes.description: Single-port record Pool. Round-robin arbitration selects at most one Queue request, validates partition ownership and returns the tagged record to that Queue Cache.

sourceEvidence.basis: Round-robin request selection chooses at most one Queue per physical cycle.
Ready is one-hot for the granted Queue.
Grant validation checks partition ownership, generation and index.

nodes.description: Each formal endpoint owns a four-entry prefetch Cache. The Cache owns storage bookkeeping and keeps its head record stable until semantic retirement.

sourceEvidence.basis: Fetch offset, Retire offset, Cache level and in-flight read state are Queue-local.
One Cache is generated for every formal Queue endpoint.

nodes.description: Tracks the next Queue-local record requested from the Shared Pool.
Advances only when the current semantic operation completes.
Tracks accepted Pool reads whose tagged response has not yet returned.
Exposes the oldest cached record until head_retire confirms semantic completion.
Each Queue Controller interprets the Cache head record, stops its scheduler counter on the exact control-cycle boundary and holds the current wait until matching completion.

sourceEvidence.basis: The Controller declares five semantic states.
scheduler_counter_ce is suppressed on the exact control-cycle hit and in all wait states.

nodes.description: Advances the local Scheduler Cycle Counter until the Cache head reaches its programmed cycle, then dispatches the semantic operation.
Holds arrival asserted until the current barrier round releases this participant.
Blocks on a matching 32-bit Event TAG; mismatched tags do not retire the record.
Holds NOTIFY until all configured participants have arrived and the barrier accepts the notifier.
Holds the 32-bit packet ordinal stable until the external packet-retired indication.
Controller scheduler_counter_ce outputs directly gate 208 MEM and 12 MXM Queue-local 32-bit counters. These counters live inside the FU subsystems, not inside QCTL System.

sourceEvidence.basis: Each MEM bank-local issue path owns a 32-bit QCTL Scheduler Cycle Counter.
Each MXM Load, Dequant and Compute path owns a 32-bit QCTL Scheduler Cycle Counter.

nodes.description: Two MEM hemispheres × 104 bank-local frontend/queue paths.
Four MXM subsystems × Load, Dequant and Compute local paths.

The participant mask defines the current round. Arrivals are idempotently accumulated; an early NOTIFY is held until every participant arrives, then one Release pulse reaches all participants and the round is cleared.

sourceEvidence.basis: Arrival state is masked and accumulated idempotently.
NOTIFY is accepted only after all participants have arrived.
Accepted NOTIFY clears the round and registers one-cycle Release.
Release-edge arrivals are not re-latched into the next round.

nodes.description: Defines exactly which Queue endpoints belong to the current barrier round.
Repeated arrival assertions set the same bit and do not create historical tokens.
NOTIFY remains blocked until all configured participants have arrived.
A one-cycle Release is broadcast to all participants, then the round is cleared without leakage.
Retains early events in eight TAG slots. A matching TAG is broadcast and releases every Controller currently waiting for that same TAG.

sourceEvidence.basis: The same matching TAG broadcast releases every waiter for that TAG.
Unmatched early events are retained in the Event Buffer.

nodes.description: An event may arrive before its waiter and remains buffered until consumed.
One matching TAG simultaneously releases all Controllers waiting for that TAG.
The Controller holds a non-zero 32-bit packet ordinal stable until mem_packet_retired_i. This is packet/data-movement completion and must not be presented as an SRAM Commit.

sourceEvidence.basis: MEM_PACKET validates a non-zero operand and exposes it as the packet ordinal.
MEMPACKET_WAIT holds the ordinal until mem_packet_retired_i.

nodes.description: The ordinal is latched when the Controller enters MEMPACKET_WAIT and remains unchanged while blocked.
External DMA/data movement owns retirement generation. QCTL consumes the final completion indication.

nodes.displayName: Formal Endpoint Map · MEM + MXM Only
nodes.description: The 220 formal QCTL endpoints are exactly 208 MEM bank-local paths and 12 MXM local paths. VXM and SXM are intentionally outside the current formal Queue numbering and direct counter-control chain.
Two hemispheres × 104 bank-local MEM frontend/queue/counter paths.
One Load path per MXM.
One Dequant path per MXM.
One Compute path per MXM.
No formal VXM QCTL endpoint or direct QCTL scheduler-counter CE mapping exists in the current cluster integration.
No formal SXM QCTL endpoint or direct QCTL scheduler-counter CE mapping exists in the current cluster integration.

interfaces.semanticDescription: Ready/valid request and response path between local instruction memory and fetch.

sourceEvidence.basis: Explicit request/response port bindings.

interfaces.name: Macro Word FIFO → Macro Decoder
interfaces.semanticDescription: 97-bit FIFO entry supplies 96-bit word plus last marker to lpu_mem_macro_decoder.

sourceEvidence.basis: Macro decoder consumes word FIFO output.

interfaces.name: Macro Decoder → Context FIFO
interfaces.semanticDescription: Decoded instruction, cycle/count/interval/stride/target/address fields are packed into a 271-bit context.

sourceEvidence.basis: Context concatenation is explicit RTL.

interfaces.name: Context FIFO → Macro Scheduler
interfaces.semanticDescription: Context FIFO output fields feed scheduler context ports.

sourceEvidence.basis: Context FIFO output is unpacked into scheduler fields.

interfaces.name: Local iMEM Fetch → Macro Decode
interfaces.semanticDescription: 96-bit word + valid/ready/last enters the macro Word FIFO and selected lpu_mem_macro_decoder path.

sourceEvidence.basis: Fetch word port bindings.

interfaces.name: Macro Scheduler → Frontend Instruction Queue
interfaces.semanticDescription: Inside each bank-local Frontend, the macro scheduler emits valid/ready, 64-bit MEM machine code and 32-bit absolute issue cycle into the final 96-bit Instruction Queue.

sourceEvidence.basis: Macro scheduler outputs bind to scheduled_instruction_*.
The same signals bind directly into u_instruction_queue.

interfaces.name: Queue Head / Schedule Match
interfaces.semanticDescription: FIFO head instruction and cycle are released only on schedule equality.

sourceEvidence.basis: Head fields and schedule match are explicit assignments.

interfaces.name: Frontend Instruction Queue → FU-local Issue Select
interfaces.semanticDescription: 104 scheduled valid/instruction/cycle lanes leave the final Instruction Queue inside each Frontend.

sourceEvidence.basis: Each complete Frontend directly drives its local_issue_* lane.

interfaces.name: Local Queue Source
interfaces.semanticDescription: Local queue vector selected when local_frontend_enable_i is asserted.

sourceEvidence.basis: Local/external mux expression.

interfaces.name: Frontend / local iMEM → Decode / Control
interfaces.semanticDescription: The combined bank-local frontend/queue paths sit south of the bank array. Their 104-lane public MEM64 issue vector reaches one adapter per lane before entering Native bank command columns.

sourceEvidence.basis: Local queue issue drives the Native execution issue vector.
Native commands enter the bank column from the south.

interfaces.name: Decode / Control → MEM Data Path
interfaces.semanticDescription: Only legal and implemented MEM64 operations are adapted into private Native32 commands for the default Native execution array.

sourceEvidence.basis: Adapter emits Native32 only when legal && implemented.

interfaces.name: Unsupported / Illegal Status
interfaces.semanticDescription: GATHER/SCATTER and opcode2 do not enter Native execution; fault status preserves the distinction between legal-unsupported and illegal.

sourceEvidence.basis: Fault and unsupported outputs are explicit.

interfaces.name: iMEM Request / Response
interfaces.semanticDescription: Ready/valid request and response path between local instruction memory and fetch.

sourceEvidence.basis: Explicit request/response port bindings.

interfaces.name: Macro Word FIFO → Macro Decoder
interfaces.semanticDescription: 97-bit FIFO entry supplies 96-bit word plus last marker to lpu_mem_macro_decoder.

sourceEvidence.basis: Macro decoder consumes word FIFO output.

interfaces.name: Macro Decoder → Context FIFO
interfaces.semanticDescription: Decoded instruction, cycle/count/interval/stride/target/address fields are packed into a 271-bit context.

sourceEvidence.basis: Context concatenation is explicit RTL.

interfaces.name: Context FIFO → Macro Scheduler
interfaces.semanticDescription: Context FIFO output fields feed scheduler context ports.

sourceEvidence.basis: Context FIFO output is unpacked into scheduler fields.

interfaces.name: Local iMEM Fetch → Macro Decode
interfaces.semanticDescription: 96-bit word + valid/ready/last enters the macro Word FIFO and selected lpu_mem_macro_decoder path.

sourceEvidence.basis: Fetch word port bindings.

interfaces.name: Macro Scheduler → Frontend Instruction Queue
interfaces.semanticDescription: Inside each bank-local Frontend, the macro scheduler emits valid/ready, 64-bit MEM machine code and 32-bit absolute issue cycle into the final 96-bit Instruction Queue.

sourceEvidence.basis: Macro scheduler outputs bind to scheduled_instruction_*.
The same signals bind directly into u_instruction_queue.

interfaces.name: Queue Head / Schedule Match
interfaces.semanticDescription: FIFO head instruction and cycle are released only on schedule equality.

sourceEvidence.basis: Head fields and schedule match are explicit assignments.

interfaces.name: Frontend Instruction Queue → FU-local Issue Select
interfaces.semanticDescription: 104 scheduled valid/instruction/cycle lanes leave the final Instruction Queue inside each Frontend.

sourceEvidence.basis: Each complete Frontend directly drives its local_issue_* lane.

interfaces.name: Local Queue Source
interfaces.semanticDescription: Local queue vector selected when local_frontend_enable_i is asserted.

sourceEvidence.basis: Local/external mux expression.

interfaces.name: Frontend / local iMEM → Decode / Control
interfaces.semanticDescription: The combined bank-local frontend/queue paths sit south of the bank array. Their 104-lane public MEM64 issue vector reaches one adapter per lane before entering Native bank command columns.

sourceEvidence.basis: Local queue issue drives the Native execution issue vector.
Native commands enter the bank column from the south.

interfaces.name: Decode / Control → MEM Data Path
interfaces.semanticDescription: Only legal and implemented MEM64 operations are adapted into private Native32 commands for the default Native execution array.

sourceEvidence.basis: Adapter emits Native32 only when legal && implemented.

interfaces.name: Unsupported / Illegal Status
interfaces.semanticDescription: GATHER/SCATTER and opcode2 do not enter Native execution; fault status preserves the distinction between legal-unsupported and illegal.

sourceEvidence.basis: Fault and unsupported outputs are explicit.

interfaces.name: East / West Stream Ingress
interfaces.semanticDescription: Physical stream interfaces feed hemisphere boundary vectors and column/tile receive data.

sourceEvidence.basis: East and west edge input ports.

notes: RTL East Edge and RTL West Edge remain separately inspectable through the top-level physical buses.

interfaces.name: Execution → East / West Stream
interfaces.semanticDescription: Tile transmit results are merged into hemisphere boundary vectors and leave through physical interfaces.

sourceEvidence.basis: East and west edge output ports.

interfaces.name: Frontend / local entry → 指令译码
interfaces.semanticDescription: Architectural handoff only: the subsystem boundary is real, while the local load adapter remains unintegrated.

interfaces.name: Transpose / Permute Issue → SXM Data Path
interfaces.semanticDescription: Resident Transpose and Permute issue channels drive the RTL-confirmed SXM control and data path.

interfaces.name: Transpose Control Wave
interfaces.semanticDescription: The Transpose command becomes four row-valid copies through lpu_control_pipeline.

interfaces.name: Registered Permute Control
interfaces.semanticDescription: The Permute command is registered once and controls the complete four-Tile bank.

interfaces.name: Uncaptured Stream Pass-through
interfaces.semanticDescription: Stream words not selected by Transpose enter the one-cycle boundary registers.

interfaces.name: Selected Stream Capture
interfaces.semanticDescription: Sixteen selected streams per Tile provide the captured transpose bytes.

interfaces.name: Transpose Capture → Tile Banks
interfaces.semanticDescription: Capture fire writes the explicit 2 × 8 × 4 × 8 byte register array.

interfaces.name: Tile Banks → Permutation Routing
interfaces.semanticDescription: A ready source Tile supplies both planes through the validated 32-lane permutation map.

interfaces.name: Registered Pass Traffic
interfaces.semanticDescription: The previous-cycle boundary register drives East-outer or West-inner.

interfaces.name: Permuted Output Traffic
interfaces.semanticDescription: Instruction-produced Permute bytes target the selected architectural boundary directly.

interfaces.semanticDescription: The FIFO head supplies one macro word plus its last marker to the decoder.

interfaces.semanticDescription: Decoded macro fields are packed into the context FIFO entry.

interfaces.name: Context FIFO → Scheduler
interfaces.semanticDescription: The context FIFO head feeds the macro scheduler.

interfaces.name: Queue Head → Schedule Match

interfaces.semanticDescription: The context FIFO head feeds the macro scheduler.

interfaces.name: Queue Head → Schedule Match
interfaces.semanticDescription: FIFO head cycle and instruction are checked before issue.

interfaces.name: Frontend / local iMEM → Macro Decode / Timed Issue
interfaces.semanticDescription: Integrated local frontends feed the three dedicated macro decode, scheduling and timed-issue paths.

interfaces.name: Decoded / Scheduled Instructions → MXM Data Path
interfaces.semanticDescription: The local coordinator selects timed Load, Dequant and Compute commands for the matrix execution slice.

interfaces.name: LOAD Frontend → Timed Queue
interfaces.semanticDescription: Valid/ready, instruction and issue-cycle enqueue path.

interfaces.name: DEQUANT Frontend → Timed Queue
interfaces.semanticDescription: Valid/ready, instruction and issue-cycle enqueue path.

interfaces.name: COMPUTE Frontend → Timed Queue
interfaces.semanticDescription: Valid/ready, instruction and issue-cycle enqueue path.

interfaces.name: Timed Queues → Coordinator
interfaces.semanticDescription: Load, dequant and compute source valid/ready/instruction/cycle paths converge in the coordinator.

interfaces.name: Coordinator → MXM Slice
interfaces.semanticDescription: Selected local/external load, dequant and compute commands drive the execution slice.

interfaces.name: Load / Dequant Row Control
interfaces.semanticDescription: Four-row Load and Dequant commands select weight-buffer updates.

interfaces.name: Compute Row Control
interfaces.semanticDescription: Four-row Compute commands select activations and accumulator destinations.

interfaces.name: Weight Store → Dot Rows
interfaces.semanticDescription: Double-buffered weight_bits and cell_valid feed every generated Dot Row.

interfaces.name: FP32 Partial Results → Shared Accumulator
interfaces.semanticDescription: result_valid, result_values, address, stream routing and clear/mode fields cross the explicit ready boundary.

interfaces.name: Frontend / local entry → 指令译码
interfaces.semanticDescription: Architectural handoff only: the direct boundary is real, while the local load adapter remains unintegrated.

interfaces.name: Resident Local / Global Issue → VXM Control
interfaces.semanticDescription: Eight local issue vectors and one global configuration vector feed the explicit VXM control instance.

interfaces.name: VXM Control → Vector Data Path
interfaces.semanticDescription: Registered configuration waves and execute pulses drive the vector tiles and stream data path.

interfaces.name: Resident Issue → VXM Control
interfaces.semanticDescription: Eight local issue vectors and one global config vector enter the explicit control instance.

interfaces.name: Configure Wave → Fixed Execute Pulse
interfaces.semanticDescription: Four-row registered configuration is followed by a one-cycle, non-retriable execute pulse when the destination Tile is ready.

interfaces.name: Hemisphere Stream Ingress
interfaces.semanticDescription: Both hemisphere boundaries enter the direction-aware bridge.

interfaces.name: Direction-selected Tile Inputs
interfaces.semanticDescription: The global flow-direction bit selects which hemisphere side supplies each Tile while stream numbers remain fixed.

interfaces.name: Private LUT Responses
interfaces.semanticDescription: Each Tile issues 4 Function × 8 Lane requests to its own private 32-SRAM LUT array.

interfaces.name: Tile Results → Opposite Boundary
interfaces.semanticDescription: Produced vectors are placed on the opposite hemisphere side according to the registered direction.

interfaces.name: Vector Results → MEM
interfaces.semanticDescription: east_to_mem valid/data vectors leave the central bridge.

interfaces.name: Central Direct → VXM Program Boundary
interfaces.semanticDescription: The real Program Boundary is connected through the Relay-bypass route, but Ready remains zero and the missing adapter prevents endpoint integration.
notes: Boundary Connected / Endpoint Not Integrated · Ready=0 · No Commit.

interfaces.name: Missing Adapter → Standalone Macro Frontend
interfaces.semanticDescription: Intentional gap: the standalone frontend unit test does not establish a Program Load connection.

interfaces.name: Simulation-only Program Bytes
interfaces.semanticDescription: Conceptual association only: the testbench supplies bytes that stand in for an external program image.
notes: No memory-array or DDR timing behavior is modeled.

interfaces.name: Request Contract → Future Adapter
interfaces.semanticDescription: An external integration layer must translate the generic request contract into the selected memory-fabric protocol.

interfaces.name: Future Adapter → Response Contract
interfaces.semanticDescription: An external integration layer must return generic response beats to the Instruction DMA.

interfaces.name: Reserve Request ID
interfaces.semanticDescription: Each accepted request enqueues its ID before the external request is considered accepted.

interfaces.name: Program Read Request
interfaces.semanticDescription: After an outstanding ID slot is reserved, the accepted loader command is presented on the generic external Program DMA request contract.

interfaces.name: Response Beat Enqueue
interfaces.semanticDescription: Each accepted response beat enters the 16-entry, 298-bit response FIFO.

interfaces.name: Response ID / Error Check
interfaces.semanticDescription: The accepted response ID is checked against the oldest outstanding ID; error is checked in parallel.

interfaces.name: Buffered Program Response
interfaces.semanticDescription: The response FIFO head is exposed to Program Load reassembly.

interfaces.name: DMA Fault Status
interfaces.semanticDescription: ID mismatch or external response error becomes a terminal fault until reset.

interfaces.name: DMA → 响应缓冲
interfaces.semanticDescription: Instruction DMA accepts and buffers the external response record before reassembly.

interfaces.name: 缓冲 → Assembler
interfaces.semanticDescription: Buffered response bytes and valid-byte keep information enter lpu_program_load_reassembler.

interfaces.name: Assembler → Word FIFO
interfaces.semanticDescription: The Reassembler emits one Program Word record into the explicit eight-entry FIFO.

interfaces.name: Word FIFO → Elastic Stage
interfaces.semanticDescription: WRITE/PRIME handoff details are contained inside this boundary; the architectural main chain crosses from the load-system Word FIFO into the Distributor Elastic Stage.

interfaces.name: Elastic Stage → Relay Chain
interfaces.semanticDescription: Scope/Destination routing feeds the West and East seven-stage Relay chains.

interfaces.name: Relay Chain → FU Frontends / local iMEM
interfaces.semanticDescription: Relay-local records terminate at MEM/MXM frontends and reach the SXM boundary; integration status remains endpoint-specific.

interfaces.name: VXM Direct · Elastic / Distributor → Frontend Boundary
interfaces.semanticDescription: The VXM route is selected from the Distributor elastic head and bypasses both Relay chains. The VXM subsystem boundary is real, but the local load adapter remains unintegrated.

interfaces.name: Command Descriptor Write
interfaces.semanticDescription: Host fields write one complete Program command descriptor.

interfaces.name: Descriptor Fetch / Command PC
interfaces.semanticDescription: The command PC selects and captures one descriptor before any external valid asserts.

interfaces.name: DMA Command · Address / Length / ID
interfaces.semanticDescription: A load descriptor launches source address, byte count and DMA ID into the Instruction DMA.

interfaces.name: Image Context Enqueue
interfaces.semanticDescription: Scope, Destination and image context pair with the matching response stream.

interfaces.name: DMA Response
interfaces.semanticDescription: Buffered response data, byte keep, last, response ID and error leave the DMA stage.

interfaces.name: Program Response Bytes + Valid-byte Mask
interfaces.semanticDescription: Only response bytes selected by response_keep enter the 64-byte reservoir.

interfaces.name: Image Context + Route Metadata
interfaces.semanticDescription: The dequeued context establishes format, image boundaries and route metadata.

interfaces.name: Compacted Bytes → Program Word
interfaces.semanticDescription: The builder consumes 12 or 16 compacted bytes for the next logical instruction word.

interfaces.name: Program Word
interfaces.semanticDescription: The complete Program Word record enters the explicit eight-entry FIFO.

interfaces.name: Word FIFO Dequeue + Route Metadata
interfaces.semanticDescription: load_word_* supplies WRITE data and route metadata to the handoff mux.

interfaces.name: Deferred PRIME Control
interfaces.semanticDescription: After loading completes, the deferred target selects a PRIME record.

interfaces.name: Distributor Input Handshake
interfaces.semanticDescription: The selected record enters the two-entry elastic stage.

interfaces.name: Buffered Program Load Record
interfaces.semanticDescription: The elastic head exposes Control, payload, Scope and Destination to route predicates.

interfaces.name: West Record
interfaces.semanticDescription: West transmits one concrete Program Record.

interfaces.name: East Record
interfaces.semanticDescription: East transmits one concrete Program Record.

interfaces.name: West R0–R6
interfaces.semanticDescription: West enters W0 and traverses seven registered stages.

interfaces.name: East R0–R6
interfaces.semanticDescription: East enters E0 and traverses seven registered stages.

interfaces.name: Integrated MEM / MXM Frontends
interfaces.semanticDescription: Relay-local records terminate in integrated MEM/MXM local iMEM/frontend paths.

interfaces.name: SXM / VXM Program Boundary
interfaces.semanticDescription: Real subsystem boundaries are connected; local load adapters remain unintegrated.

interfaces.name: Commit
interfaces.semanticDescription: Accepted integrated writes return ordered status.

interfaces.name: START
interfaces.semanticDescription: Controller lifecycle starts integrated FU-local frontends.

interfaces.name: Fault
interfaces.semanticDescription: Endpoint and frontend faults return to lifecycle control.

interfaces.name: Program Reset / Transport Flush
interfaces.semanticDescription: Program Reset clears transport and frontend state.

interfaces.name: Shared Pool → Per-Queue Cache

states.name: IDLE
states.statement: Reads the current Head Record and keeps CE high only for nonblocking or already-completed work.

states.name: SYNC_WAIT
states.statement: Holds the Queue until the Participant-Mask Barrier broadcasts Release.

states.name: EVENT_WAIT
states.statement: Holds the Queue until the 32-bit TAG Event broadcast matches the saved operand.

states.name: NOTIFY_WAIT
states.statement: Keeps an early NOTIFY request asserted; retirement waits for the current round to release.

states.name: MEMPACKET_WAIT
states.statement: Keeps the packet ordinal stable until external mem_packet_retired_i.

barrier.participantMask: Only Queue IDs selected by participant_mask_i participate in the current barrier round.
barrier.arrival: Arrival is an idempotent per-round bit mask, not a token counter.
barrier.notify: An early NOTIFY remains pending and cannot retire before every configured participant arrives.
barrier.release: A successful NOTIFY emits one-cycle Release directly to all participants.
barrier.roundIsolation: Arrival state is cleared on Release and held clear across the Release edge, so consecutive rounds do not leak history.

eventBuffer.statement: The independent Event Buffer retains early DMA completion TAGs outside every Controller; one matching TAG broadcast may release every waiting Controller with that TAG.

memPacket.retirement: MEM_PACKET ordinal remains stable while waiting and retires only through external mem_packet_retired_i.
memPacket.sramCommitRelationship: Packet retirement is not SRAM Commit. QCTL consumes only the final data-completion event; generation of the final SRAM Commit event remains in DMA / data movement.

pipeline.title: MEM Macro Scheduler · Context Expansion Pipeline
pipeline.summary: The MEM Scheduler validates and converts the Context FIFO head, admits it directly into an originally free Active Context slot, then selects work ahead of the absolute issue cycle and emits one MEM base instruction into the paired Instruction Queue. outer_cycle_transition advances from the previous row final issue to the next row first issue; outer_spatial_transition applies the matching address or operand transition.
pipeline.inputLabel: 271 bit Context · ready/valid from Context FIFO
pipeline.outputLabel: 64 bit instruction + 32-bit issue cycle → Frontend Instruction Queue
pipeline.timingNote: Registered ownership boundaries are the upstream Context FIFO, Active Context state and the FU-local Instruction Queue. The MEM Scheduler has no second ingress register: context_admit_fire is the direct Context FIFO handshake into an originally free Active Context slot. Active Context advances only on schedule_select_fire, when the Instruction Queue accepts the generated instruction. outer_cycle_transition advances from the previous row final issue to the next row first issue; outer_spatial_transition applies the matching address or operand transition.

steps.name: Context FIFO Head
steps.description: Observe the current Context FIFO output fields directly; the FIFO retains the head while context_ready_o is low.

steps.name: Validation + Conversion
steps.description: Check target, native instruction, loop counts, intervals, strides, address range and absolute deadline while deriving the Active Context schedule state directly from context_*_i.

steps.name: Direct Active Context Admission
steps.description: context_admit_fire writes the validated and converted Context directly into the first originally free Active Context slot.

steps.name: Active Context State
steps.description: Store up to 4 active Contexts with remaining loop counts, next issue cycle and normalized outer transition state.

steps.name: Lookahead Due Select
steps.description: Compare next-issue cycles against schedule_cycle + 2 and detect conflicts, missed generation or overflow.

steps.name: Base Instruction Generate
steps.description: Apply the current induced address and form the 64 bit MEM instruction.

steps.name: Instruction Queue Handoff
steps.description: schedule_select_fire transfers the timed instruction to Frontend Instruction Queue; only this accepted handshake advances or retires the Context.

pipeline.summary: RUN_2D packet words are collected, reordered into one logical payload, validated and converted into one normalized scheduling Context.
pipeline.inputLabel: 96-bit macro word · ready/valid from Word FIFO
pipeline.timingNote: Functional processing pipeline: packet collection and decode_pending are registered phases; the Context output remains stable until the Context FIFO accepts it.

steps.name: Packet Word Intake
steps.description: Accept 96-bit macro word words from the frontend Word FIFO.

steps.name: Logical Packet Assembly
steps.description: Collect the multi-word RUN_2D packet and close physical header/subtype gaps into one logical payload.

steps.name: Header + Reserved Validation
steps.description: Check opcode/subtype, required word count and reserved fields before any Context is exposed.

steps.name: Schedule + Instruction Decode
steps.description: Extract base/wait cycle, inner/outer loop fields and the FU-specific base instruction.

steps.name: Registered Context Output
steps.description: Hold the complete 608-bit Context stable until the Context FIFO accepts it.

specs.label: Internal issue FIFO
specs.value: None · queue is the register boundary

pipeline.title: Transpose Scheduler · Context Expansion Pipeline
pipeline.summary: The Scheduler captures and admits a decoded Context through distinct ownership boundaries, retains its loop/timing state, selects work ahead of the absolute issue cycle and emits one FU base instruction into the paired Instruction Queue. outer_cycle_transition advances from the previous row final issue to the next row first issue.
pipeline.inputLabel: 608 bit Context · ready/valid from Context FIFO
pipeline.outputLabel: 416 bit instruction + 32-bit issue cycle → SXM Issue Queue
pipeline.timingNote: Registered ownership boundaries are Context ingress, Active Context state and the FU-local Instruction Queue. context_capture_fire captures Context FIFO data; context_admit_fire moves the ingress record into a slot that was already free before the current edge. Active Context advances only on schedule_select_fire, when the queue accepts the generated instruction. outer_cycle_transition advances from the previous row final issue to the next row first issue.

steps.name: Context Ingress Register
steps.description: context_capture_fire captures one Context through ready/valid without exposing Active Context storage latency upstream.

steps.name: Validate + Admit
steps.description: context_admit_fire checks target, instruction, loop counts, transitions and deadline lead time, then writes only a slot that was already free before the current edge.

steps.name: Active Context State
steps.description: Store up to 1 active Context with remaining loop counts, next issue cycle and normalized outer transition state.

steps.name: Lookahead Due Select
steps.description: Compare next-issue cycles against schedule_cycle + 2 and detect conflicts, missed generation or overflow.

steps.name: Base Instruction Generate
steps.description: Apply the current induced operand/address and form the 416 bit FU instruction.

steps.name: Instruction Queue Handoff
steps.description: schedule_select_fire transfers the timed instruction to SXM Issue Queue; only this accepted handshake advances or retires the Context.

stages.role: Boundary connected; local load adapter not integrated
